source_text: Non qui virtute iudicii delicta vitasset; sed qui felicitate carnis a nostris sensibus sequestratae, cupiditatem vitiorum sentire nequivisset.
pass_a_gloss: Not one who by the virtue of judgment had avoided offenses; but one who by the luck of a flesh sequestered from our senses had been unable to feel the desire of vices.
pass_b_english: He was not, on this account, someone who avoided offenses through the strength of his judgment, but someone who could not feel the desire for vices because his flesh had the advantage of being separated from our sensations.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
